rule: Partition-mapper methods that format upstream/downstream keys must use timezone-aware datetimes anchored to the mapper's configured timezone, not naive datetimes, so the scheduler waits on the correct keys.
trigger: diff adds or modifies a `to_upstream()` or `to_downstream()` method in a partition mapper that calls `datetime.strptime` or `timedelta` arithmetic without attaching `self._timezone`
rationale: Naive datetime arithmetic in partition mappers produces wrong upstream keys when the mapper timezone is not UTC or when `input_format` includes `%z`, causing the scheduler to wait on keys that never arrive.

evidence.excerpt: generated upstream keys can be wrong when mapper timezone is not UTC

rule: When a method is decorated with `@provider_info_cache`, update its docstring to reflect the cached semantics; do not carry over "use this to avoid triggering caching" language written for the former uncached inner method.
trigger: diff moves a docstring from an uncached helper onto a `@provider_info_cache`-decorated method, or adds a `@provider_info_cache` decorator without revising the docstring
rationale: The 'do not want to trigger caching' language becomes misleading after the method itself is decorated with the cache; reviewers flag this as a stale docstring.

evidence.excerpt: "do not want to trigger caching" language no longer makes sense here

rule: New task-clearing behaviour flags (e.g. only_failed, only_running, new fields of the same kind) must be implemented inside `clear_task_instances`, not scattered across other call sites.
trigger: diff adds a new boolean filter field to a task-clearing code path and handles it outside of `clear_task_instances`
rationale: Consistency with existing fields (only_failed, only_running) is required; the reviewer explicitly asks for the logic to live in `clear_task_instances` so all clearing semantics are in one place.

evidence.excerpt: new field should behave like other fields, handled in clear_task_instances

rule: In `create_dagrun()`, resolve the requested bundle version first and then validate partition key against the resolved DAG version, not against `self` (which is always the latest DAG).
trigger: diff adds or modifies `create_dagrun()` and calls `self.validate_partition_key(partition_key)` before resolving `bundle_version` to a `DagVersion`
rationale: Validating against `self` (latest version) causes false failures for partitioned older bundle versions when the latest version is not partitioned.

evidence.excerpt: `bundle_version="v1"` can still fail for a partitioned v1 if latest v2 is not partitioned

rule: Custom sentinel / non-JSON-serializable types used in template fields must implement a `serialize()` method matching the pattern established by `SetDuringExecution`, so `serialize_template_field` does not fall back to `str()`.
trigger: diff introduces a new sentinel class (e.g. `ArgNotSet`, `NOTSET`-style) in airflow-core without a `serialize()` method
rationale: `serialize_template_field` in `helpers.py` falls back to `str()` when an object has no `serialize()` method; adding `serialize()` fixes the template-field serialization path without changing `__repr__`.

evidence.excerpt: `SetDuringExecution` already handles this by defining a `serialize()` method

rule: TaskGroup `topological_sort()` must not rebuild the full DAG-level group mapping on every recursive call; build the mapping once and pass it through to nested calls to avoid O(G²) traversal cost.
trigger: diff modifies `topological_sort()` in `taskgroup.py` (core or Task SDK) and constructs a group-lookup dict inside the function body without accepting it as a parameter
rationale: Grid/Graph serializers call `topological_sort()` recursively for every nested TaskGroup; rebuilding the full mapping each time changes cost from O(G) to O(G²).

evidence.excerpt: G non-empty groups performs approximately G full traversals of the same G-group tree

rule: Do not open a new `create_session` block inside a method when an equivalent query can be routed through an existing model method (e.g. `XComModel.get_many`) that accepts the session.
trigger: diff adds a `with create_session()` block inside a method that already has access to a session parameter or can delegate to an existing model query method
rationale: Re-using the model's `get_many` path avoids a redundant session block and keeps session management consistent with the rest of the ORM layer.

evidence.excerpt: call `session.execute` in `get_many` method; don't need `create_session` block here

rule: Compatibility shims for deprecated `settings.*` attributes (e.g. `SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN_ASYNC`) must be guarded by `block_orm_access` the same way as their `SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN` counterpart, so task code cannot bypass the metadatabase access block.
trigger: diff adds or modifies a `__getattr__` branch in `settings.py` for a `*_ASYNC` or secondary connection attribute without a `block_orm_access` guard
rationale: `block_orm_access()` is meaningless if task/DAG code can still read the real async connection string via the unguarded shim.

evidence.excerpt: task/DAG code could still retrieve real async connection string, undermining `block_orm_access()`

rule: SQLite in-memory detection in engine-configuration code must use SQLAlchemy URL parsing (check dialect and database target), not string equality against `"sqlite://"` or `"sqlite:///:memory:"`.
trigger: diff checks for in-memory SQLite using `==` or `in` with string literals `"sqlite://"` or `"sqlite:///:memory:"`
rationale: Connection URLs may include driver prefixes (`+pysqlite`), query params (`?cache=shared`), or alternative in-memory forms (`file::memory:`); equality checks miss these and incorrectly apply `pool_size`/`max_overflow` to `SingletonThreadPool`.

evidence.excerpt: only matches exact strings; connection URLs can include driver prefix or query params

rule: When `map_index == -1` is used as a sentinel in `TaskScope`, its semantics ("match all" vs "match only the non-mapped row") must be identical across all methods that filter on it; inconsistent sentinel semantics must be replaced with an explicit boolean flag.
trigger: diff adds or modifies methods in a `TaskScope`-accepting state class where some methods skip the `map_index` filter for `-1` and others apply an exact-match filter for `-1`
rationale: Opposite semantics for the same sentinel value across sibling methods (delete vs clear) is a foot-gun; an explicit `clear_all_map_indices: bool = False` flag removes the ambiguity.

evidence.excerpt: same `TaskScope(map_index=-1)`, opposite semantics: delete only touches non-mapped row, clear wipes every map index

rule: State-store write methods that check for an existing row then insert must use a single database-level UPSERT (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`) instead of SELECT-then-INSERT to prevent race-condition `IntegrityError`.
trigger: diff adds a state-write method that does `session.get(...)` or a SELECT followed by `session.add(row)` for the same primary/unique key
rationale: Two concurrent calls can both see `None` and both attempt INSERT; one gets an `IntegrityError`. A DB-level UPSERT is atomic and cheaper (single round-trip).

evidence.excerpt: Two concurrent calls for the same (scope, key) can both INSERT; one gets IntegrityError

rule: Asset-store upsert calls must omit writer-attribution columns from the update set when `kind is None`, so that an attribution-less write does not silently overwrite existing attribution data with NULL.
trigger: diff modifies `_set_asset_store` or a `_build_upsert_stmt` call for `AssetStoreModel` and unconditionally includes `last_updated_by_*` columns in the update dict
rationale: A plain `set()` (kind=None) reaches the upsert with no writer info; listing those columns in the update set overwrites previously recorded attribution with NULL on conflict.

evidence.excerpt: a plain `set()` on an AssetScope overwrites previously recorded writer info back to NULL

rule: State-set constants in `dependencies_states.py` must be named to reflect their semantic role (ACTIVE_STATES for anything-still-in-flight, EXECUTION_STATES for actively-executing tasks), not after the implementation detail that defines them.
trigger: diff introduces a new `frozenset` or `set` of `TaskInstanceState` values in `ti_deps/dependencies_states.py` with a name ending in `_EXECUTION_STATES` when the set includes `DEFERRED` or other non-executing in-flight states
rationale: EXECUTION_STATES already exists for tasks in execution; a superset that includes DEFERRED should be ACTIVE_STATES to distinguish 'logically in-flight' from 'actively executing'.

evidence.excerpt: call this ACTIVE_STATES to clarify these states are used when checking if a task is active

rule: All public `Timetable` method overrides must include an explicit return-type annotation.
trigger: diff adds or overrides a public method on a class that inherits from `Timetable` without a `-> ReturnType` annotation
rationale: Reviewer suggested the return type annotation in a code suggestion; timetable public API is part of the Airflow provider contract and must be fully typed.

evidence.excerpt: suggestion adds `-> DagRunInfo | None` return annotation to `next_dagrun_info_v2`

rule: Do not add `__all__` when a symbol is already re-exported via the `import X as X` pattern; the `as Name` form is the single authoritative re-export mechanism in airflow-core.
trigger: diff adds both `from module import Foo as Foo` and also lists `Foo` inside `__all__` in the same file
rationale: In airflow-core, `import X as X` is the designated public-re-export idiom; duplicating it in `__all__` is redundant and was explicitly rejected by a reviewer.

evidence.excerpt: I don't think we want `StartTriggerArgs as StartTriggerArgs` and `__all__`, just the former is enough

rule: When `RunTrigger` or any callback trigger resolves a DAG module by hashed path, the absence of a run-version pin and cross-host path skew must be explicitly documented as a known limitation in the code if not addressed.
trigger: diff adds a trigger or callback that resolves a DAG file via `get_unique_dag_module_name` (sha1 of absolute path) without a `bundle_version` or run-version identifier on the trigger payload
rationale: `get_all_dag_bundles()` returns current-version bundles; a triggerer host with a different bundle path won't hash-match the minted name, causing the callback to end FAILED silently.

evidence.excerpt: cross-version / cross-host path skew: worth a code comment

rule: New `SharedStreamManager` stream types added for provider upstreams that require an ack/commit side-effect (e.g. Kafka offset commit) must not use the unidirectional `filter_shared_stream` API; scope such PRs to read-only/idempotent upstreams or extend the API with an ack path first.
trigger: diff adds a `open_shared_stream` implementation that commits, acks, or advances a cursor after a filter accept, routed through the existing one-way `filter_shared_stream` channel
rationale: `filter_shared_stream` is one-way; there is no path for a subscriber to signal 'accepted' back to the producer, so commit/ack side-effects cannot be triggered after filter acceptance.

evidence.excerpt: filter_shared_stream is a one-way channel; no path back for upstreams needing ack/commit

rule: Do not expose a new public property on `CronMixin` (core timetables) solely to serve SDK-side consumers; SDK timetables already expose their own API surface and the core mixin's public API must have at least one in-core consumer.
trigger: diff adds a `@property` to `CronMixin` or another core timetable base class with no reference site in airflow-core code
rationale: A `timezone` property was added to `CronMixin` to serve `dag_clear`, but after the refactor `dag_clear` no longer reads it; SDK timetables expose their own `timezone`. Dead public API on a core mixin should be removed.

evidence.excerpt: public `timezone` property has no consumers in core; PR-description bullet justifying it is stale
